newsitem.title: UK: Tschudi & Eitzen alters name to Waterfront.
newsitem.headline: Tschudi & Eitzen alters name to Waterfront.

text.p: Norwegian bulk shipping group Tschudi & Eitzen Shipping said Tuesday it will change its name to Waterfront Shipping ASA tomorrow. The new Oslo Bourse ticker code will be WAT.
The name change marks the end of involvement in the firm of its founders Felix Tschudi and Axel Eitzen.

Tschudi & Eitzen Shipping owns a modern fleet of panamax oil/bulk/ore carriers (OBOs) and long range petroleum product carriers. Most were acquired from companies associated with collapsed Danish shipbuilder Burmeister & Wain.
Subsidiary Tschudi & Eitzen OBO Carriers will also change its name to Waterfront OBO Carriers.

At the end of June, Felix Tschudi and Axel Eitzen sold their entire remaining holding of 5.5 million Tschudi & Eitzen shares at 7.20 Norwegian crowns each after effectively losing control of the firm.
Norwegian shipping investor Christen Sveaas lifted his stake in Tschudi & Eitzen Shipping to 44.99 percent in May after buying a further 7.1m shares through Viking Supply Ships, which he controls.
Tschudi & Eitzen Shipping's annual general meeting on June 30 voted to terminate its ship management contract with a company controlled by Felix Tschudi and Axel Eitzen.
The meeting re-elected Sveaas to the board, and elected Christen Wikborg chairman.

Felix Tschudi and Axel Eitzen continue to control a ship management business and four panamax OBOs. They also control a 50 percent stake in Estonian Shipping Company (ESCO), currently in the process of being privatised.
The new name is not related to Waterfront Shipping Company Ltd, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Methanex Corp.
